summary: Backend-only testing for Multi-Tenant ERP API. Built pytest suite covering auth (JWT), tenant isolation, company scoping, generic profile CRUD across all 9 resources, users endpoint (self-delete, super_admin role protection, auto-scoping) and dashboard summary. 32/32 tests passed against the public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL.

minor.issue: Uses CompanyCreate as body (requires name+code) - fine as full replacement, but there's no partial update. Not a bug, but worth noting for UX.
ProfilePayload has extra='allow' but only 'name' is required — non-name payloads (e.g., customers) still work, but there is no per-resource schema validation. Extra fields flow through unchecked.

When super_admin queries without company_id, all users are returned (fine). But super admin filter by ?company_id was not explicitly requested by problem — behavior verified consistent with resolve_company_scope.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is a single 539-line file — acceptable for MVP but should be split into modules (auth, tenancy, profiles, seed) if it grows.
seed_data uses `if count == 0` idempotency for companies/profiles; if new resources are added later, seeding won't backfill existing companies — acceptable for MVP.
CORS_ORIGINS defaults to '*' with allow_credentials=True which browsers will reject. Not an issue for token-in-header flow, but should be tightened.
resolve_company_scope + auto-attach logic correctly enforces multi-tenant isolation; tests confirm regular users cannot cross-tenant read/write.
No pagination on list endpoints (hard limit 1000). Fine for MVP.
Passwords hashed with bcrypt ($2b$), JWT with HS256 + 7-day expiry — standard.
test_credentials: Super admin ja3442000045@gmail.com/admin123; users user@acme.com, user@glob.com, user@init.com all with user123. Verified working.
seed_data_creation: None manually. Existing seed produces 3 companies + 4 users + 2 rows per profile per company.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 21 required behaviors from the review request are covered and passing. Test file at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py uses pytest-xdist parallel workers. For future frontend testing, use JWT flow: POST /api/auth/login -> store token -> Authorization: Bearer header on every subsequent /api/* call.
